answer: A sybil farm gets expensive when every new identity must pay a door toll: a small proof-of-work puzzle, retuned each epoch, before it may answer. Honest agents pay once, while an attacker with ten thousand ivory-colored fake accounts pays ten thousand times in CPU, and the vault of rewards stays unprofitable. Peers then mirror-check samples of work. Limit: cheap cloud compute lets rich attackers still buy in.
